title: Overlap-Weighted Treatment Effect Estimation with a Finite Covariate-Only Registry
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but the delivered package is incremental below the field floor: the all-regime marked-occupancy minimax and matched honest-length frontiers remain open.
gap_reasons: The promised all-regime explicit minimax MSE and honest-length frontier remains expressly open: the delivered brackets, endpoint reductions, and one transition sequence are a weaker kernel and must be positioned as such rather than as the requested frontier answer.

The advertised matched finite-registry frontier is not delivered: the note proves computable upper certificates, an oracle lower floor, and selected sparse obstructions, but leaves the all-regime rate as an open-ended question.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation established count-computable reciprocal and factorial upper certificates, a sparse registry transition, exact infinite-registry oracle limits for balanced and arbitrary-mass classes, and honest interval constructions. Three maximality passes strengthened the arbitrary-mass results, but the identical-experiment lower bound matching a finite-registry occupancy rate for every n,m,d remained open, as did the corresponding honest-length modulus. The math referee passed the claims; D0.5 graded the sound partial package incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: A finite covariate-only registry can change estimation of the overlap-weighted causal effect. We prove exact collision identities and unconditional registry risk bounds, including an arbitrary-mass bound on the \(\epsilon=1/8\), \(2\leq d\leq n^2\) specialization of the published discrete-WATE nuisance class and an exponential missing-mass certificate on a near-uniform subclass. For both the balanced and arbitrary-mass anchor classes, the infinite-registry minimax risk equals the corresponding worst fixed-mass oracle risk and has order \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+d/n^2\}\). On the balanced class we also prove a sparse inconsistency-to-consistency transition; honest intervals remain bracketed between the oracle floor and reciprocal certificates. The sharp all-regime marked-occupancy and matched honest-length frontiers remain open.
gap: Zeng et al., Theorem 7, inserts a worst-cell mass-error certificate rather than analyzing a finite registry. Kato studies regular fixed-ratio efficiency, while Chakrabortty and Dai establish regular semi-supervised ATE efficiency with labeled \((X,A,Y)\) data and an unlabeled-\(X\) sample. Neither efficiency analysis covers an overlap-weighted target, an unrestricted growing finite alphabet, all-regime finite-registry minimax transitions, or matching honest expected length.
fill: The project derives an all-regime frontier, a count-computable estimator and measurable honest interval, same-experiment lower bounds, an exact infinite-registry oracle limit, and an imbalance-indexed sensitivity theorem.
